WEB-ADMIN-01 #382 deterministic browser transcript (2026-09-21 KST)

Evidence boundaries
-------------------
This is a real headed Chromium run against tests/web_management_browser_fixture.py,
an independent synthetic HTTP fixture. It does not run AgentService, a real Telegram
ingest/delivery path, a model/provider, a connector, or any external effect. The
separate executable Python test
test_synthetic_telegram_request_reaches_web_read_models_without_web_chat covers
the injected Telegram service/read-model path. The browser fixture marks its own
channel as telegram:fixture-owner only so the renderer's provenance projection can
be inspected; it is not evidence of live or service-backed Telegram operation.

Prerequisite and server (terminal 1, repository root)
-----------------------------------------------------
  command -v npx
  python3 tests/web_management_browser_fixture.py --port 18782

Observed server output:
  fixture-only http://127.0.0.1:18782

-------------------------------------------
  PWCLI=/Users/jongtaelee/.codex/skills/playwright/scripts/playwright_cli.sh
  bash "$PWCLI" open http://127.0.0.1:18782/#tasks --headed
  bash "$PWCLI" resize 1280 900
  bash "$PWCLI" snapshot

Observed coherent task projection:
  list status: 진행 중
  outcome heading/text: 진행 중 / 새 이벤트를 기다리고 있습니다.
  no terminal result was rendered beside the active status.

  - the selected timeline updated from one to two events without reselection;
  - the first event remained expanded and still showed 첫 이벤트 after the
    event-driven rerender and three subsequent polling intervals;
  - status/outcome remained coherently 진행 중; the succeeded event was an
    event state, not a fabricated terminal task result;

    synthetic fixture channel described in the evidence boundary above.

Unsaved Telegram field plus browser back/forward (A7/A8)

Starting from records after the steps above:

  bash "$PWCLI" eval \
    'el => JSON.stringify({focused:document.activeElement===el,value:el.value,start:el.selectionStart,end:el.selectionEnd})' e162

Observed after three polls:
  {"test_requests": 0, "apply_requests": 0, "events": 2, "task_polls": 3}
  {"focused":true,"value":"fixture-unsaved-token","start":19,"end":19}

First positively verify that the fixture observer sees and identifies every relevant
mutating verb (the fixture rejects these probes with 405 after recording them):

  curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X PUT -d '{}' \
    http://127.0.0.1:18782/api/observer-probe
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X PATCH -d '{}' \
    http://127.0.0.1:18782/api/observer-probe
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X DELETE -d '{}' \
    http://127.0.0.1:18782/api/observer-probe
  curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18782/control/requests

Observed positive-control output:
  405
  405
  405
  {"requests":[{"method":"PUT","path":"/api/observer-probe"},
  {"method":"PATCH","path":"/api/observer-probe"},
  {"method":"DELETE","path":"/api/observer-probe"}]}

Then reset the proven observer, traverse actual browser history, and inspect the
same unsaved field and every application request made during pane/history entry:

  curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' \
    http://127.0.0.1:18782/control/reset-observation
  bash "$PWCLI" go-back
  bash "$PWCLI" go-back
  bash "$PWCLI" go-forward
  bash "$PWCLI" go-forward
  sleep 3
  bash "$PWCLI" eval \
    'el => JSON.stringify({value:el.value,visible:!el.closest("form").hidden,url:location.hash})' e162
  curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18782/control/requests

Observed:
  {"value":"fixture-unsaved-token","visible":true,"url":"#settings/external"}
  The request log contained only GET /favicon.ico, /api/tasks, /api/home,
  /api/state, and /api/personal-space entries. It contained no POST, PUT,
  PATCH, or DELETE application request. Because the positive control above proves
  that all four mutating verbs are recorded, their absence is meaningful. The reset
  control request is deliberately excluded from the application log. Thus pane
  entry and history navigation were observed read-only, not inferred from source
  strings.

R5/R6 deterministic behavior and browser request counts
---------------------------------------------------------
The executable Node check in test_source_derived_task_record_and_model_regressions
starts an unresolved old-key test, changes only the credential revision, resolves
the old success, and asserts it is rejected. It then tests the new draft and applies
once, asserting test_requests == 2 and save_requests == 1. This is executable async
behavior, not a string assertion.

In a fresh browser-fixture process, direct interaction also observed:
  - changing only the key disabled apply and displayed 다시 테스트하세요;
  - testing the new key enabled apply;
  - applying once produced /control/counts values test_requests=2 and
    apply_requests=1, proving there was no hidden third test.

No credential in this transcript is real; fixture-unsaved-token is inert text and
was never submitted.

Exact-head review repairs: unassigned result, preset, capability, mobile delete
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
In a fresh fixture process at 1280x900, the project detail rendered the completed
Telegram fixture job with no workspace_id as:

  미지정 작업 · fixture project result
  완료 결과 저장

The fixture intentionally omits workspace_id from both Telegram jobs. This is
renderer evidence only; no live Telegram or connector was used.

For the OpenRouter preset regression, the headed browser interaction was:

  fill API 키 with secret-that-must-clear
  click 도구 지원 무료 모델 보기
  click Fixture Free · fixture/free
  evaluate the API 키/provider/endpoint/model controls

Observed result:
  {"value":"","provider":"compatible","endpoint":"https://openrouter.ai/api/v1","model":"fixture/free"}

For the local capability lifecycle, entering 외부 연결 rendered the enabled
google-drive-read fixture capability. Clicking 일시 정지 first rendered an explicit
google-drive-read pause preview and 확인/취소 controls. Only after clicking 확인 did
the UI render paused and 다시 시작. /control/requests recorded two POST
/api/settings/request entries (draft, then confirm); no connector was contacted.

At 390x844, the browser searched durable-key, opened the only matching record,
clicked 삭제 and then 삭제 확인. The fixture accepted the real DELETE and the
post-delete browser evaluation returned:

  {"detailClass":"panel detail","backVisible":false,"empty":true}

Thus deleting the last matching row exits the fixed mobile-detail overlay and
returns to the visible empty list. This remains deterministic fixture evidence.

Polling disclosures, OAuth popup handoff, and empty mobile tasks
----------------------------------------------------------------
At 1280x900, the headed browser expanded both 실행 상세 and its nested 원래 요청
보기 disclosure. The fixture appended a second event and the browser waited through
three polling intervals. The post-poll evaluation observed:

  {"technical":true,"original":true,"events":2}

At 390x844, the browser selected the only task to enter its fixed detail overlay.
POST /control/empty-tasks then made the next read return no ordinary tasks. After
polling, the evaluation observed:

  {"detailClass":"panel detail","empty":true}

The task overlay therefore exited to the visible empty task list.

For the same-origin OpenRouter callback contract, the main headed page stored an
inert fixture flow, placed `stale-secret` in the form, and opened the fixture callback
popup at `/?code=fixture-code&state=fixture-state`. The popup POSTed only to the
local fixture `/api/openrouter/connect`, signalled its opener, and closed. The opener
then cleared and reloaded the stale form. Its evaluation observed:

  {"popupClosed":true,"key":"","provider":"compatible","model":"fixture/connected","feedback":"OpenRouter 연결 결과를 저장했습니다."}

No real OpenRouter account, credential, provider request, or external network effect
was used; `stale-secret`, the code, state, and verifier are inert fixture strings.

OAuth invalidates an already-enabled exact-draft proof
-----------------------------------------------------
In a fresh headed run, the direct form was filled with `prior-tested-key` and its
explicit fixture test completed. Before OAuth, the browser observed:

  {"beforeOAuthApplyDisabled":false,"key":"prior-tested-key"}

The same inert local callback flow above then completed. After the popup signalled
and closed, the opener observed:

  {"popupClosed":true,"afterOAuthApplyDisabled":true,"key":"","provider":"compatible","model":"fixture/connected","modelFeedback":"연결 결과가 바뀌었습니다. 적용 전에 다시 테스트하세요."}

Thus the prior tested draft cannot be applied after OAuth changes the stored
connection, including same-destination credential replacement. This used only the
local fixture; no provider call or live credential was involved.

Project count and bounded capability controls
---------------------------------------------
In a fresh headed fixture run, the project row initially showed 0개 완료 결과.
After saving the eligible unassigned result, the browser fetched Personal Space and
immediately observed the durable saved-result count rather than the job assignment:

  {"workspaceRow":"1개 완료 결과","savedResults":1}

The executable Node regression separately proves that an older out-of-order project
response is rejected when either its selected ID or request sequence is stale. It
also proves that `isolated-runtime-placeholder` receives no lifecycle buttons while
the four exact capability IDs understood by the existing settings parser retain
their valid controls. These are owned frontend/fixture observations only.
